analysis.investment_thesis: Neetu Yoshi is a classic fast-grower story — revenue CAGR of 142% (5→71 Cr), ROE 51%, ROCE 46%, and PEG well under 1 on trailing growth. But it's a tiny, newly-listed castings & forgings microcap with negative FCF and a short operating history, so the story is exciting but unproven.
key_strengths: Explosive growth: revenue 5→71 Cr in 3 years, PAT 0→16 Cr; operating margin jumped to ~32%
Capital efficiency is outstanding — ROE 51%, ROCE 46%, debt modest (borrowings 14 Cr vs equity 123 Cr)
Promoter holding high at 70%, fresh IPO capital (reserves 3→104 Cr) funding expansion in a tailwind sector (railway/industrial castings)
key_risks: Negative FCF every year (FY25 FCF -3 Cr); growth funded by IPO cash, not self-sustaining yet
Incorporated Jan 2020 — no cycle-tested track record in a cyclical castings/forgings industry
Customer/product concentration unknown; commoditized ferrous products vulnerable to steel price swings and margin compression
red_flags: Total assets tripled 38→144 Cr in one year — heavy capex with FCF still negative
Micro-cap with low float and potential liquidity/volatility issues post-IPO
analysis.detailed_analysis:
What's the story? A brand-new (2020) ferrous castings maker that scaled revenue 14x in three years and earns world-class returns on capital (ROE 51%, ROCE 46%). At P/E 20 against triple-digit trailing growth, the PEG is optically under 0.2 — my kind of setup. The sector tailwind (Indian railways, capex cycle, defense forgings) is visible and real, and promoter skin-in-the-game at 70% aligns incentives. If FY26 revenue hits ~100 Cr and PAT ~22-25 Cr, you're paying ~12-13x forward on a 40%+ ROCE compounder — that's how ten-baggers start.

But Lynch also says "know what you own." Castings & forgings is cyclical, commoditized, and working-capital heavy — the -3 Cr FCF at 16 Cr PAT tells me receivables/inventory are eating cash. With only 4 years of data and the company fresh off its IPO (equity jumped 20→123 Cr), I can't yet verify execution through a downturn or confirm whether growth is organic or order-book-front-loaded. I'd put this on the watchlist, track 2-3 quarters of sustained OCF conversion and margin stability, and buy on proof — not on the pitch. A 6 reflects genuine excitement tempered by the short track record.
